title: Mosaic Halo partner fit & pilot scoping
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Mosaic Halo to evaluate channel reseller fit for GPU-backed inference. Discussed deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), security/compliance needs (SOC2, KMS), pilot success metrics, and preliminary pricing/commit structure. Agreed next steps for pilot scoping and technical deep dive.
topics: Pilot scope: target workloads, SLA expectations
Network/topology: VPC peering, private control plane
Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs
Performance: quantization, batching, KV cache, routing policies

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 63 minutes | Attendees: Samir Patel, Leah Graves (Redwood); Daniel Kim, Priya Rao, Marco Silva (Mosaic Halo)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed channel partnership fit and pilot framing. High-level interest in offering Redwood Dedicated via Mosaic sales motion; Mosaic looking for predictable SLAs and pricing margins. Security and network design are blockers to close pilot.

[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, we really appreciate it. Quick roll call and then i'll hand to Leah for a short tech overview, sound good?
[00:14] Daniel (Mosaic Halo - Partnerships): Yep good, thanks Samir. Daniel here, Priya and Marco are on.
[00:22] Priya (Mosaic Halo - Cloud Architect): Hey all.
[00:26] Marco (Mosaic Halo - CTO): Morning.
[00:29] Leah (Redwood SE): Cool, i'll keep the tech part high level first, then we'll dig into the pilot asks. So Redwood provides hosted APIs, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem options. For partners doing reseller motion we often recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput and easier margins, but there are some tradeoffs—
[00:46] Leah (cont): latency vs cost, right; Dedicated gives you better predictability across RPS spikes, hosted is easiest to go to market quickly.
[00:57] Daniel: For Mosaic's reseller channel we want something we can package as part of our managed offering. We get asked a lot about data controls and auditability. SOC2 is required for a chunk of our customers, and anything above $250k ARR has to be in a VPC or private control plane.
[01:14] Samir: Totally, we've done similar partner pilots. We can offer Private (VPC) deployments where the control plane is customer-managed and keys are in their KMS/HSM. Audit logs and exportable traces are standard. We also have an enterprise SLA for Dedicated that we can surface in the term sheet.
[01:32] Priya: On the VPC side I'd like to understand peering/topology — do you support VPC peering, AWS Transit, or direct connect? Also curious about egress patterns, NAT, and whether we need to permit any public endpoints.
[01:45] Leah: We support VPC peering and customer-managed VPNs. For higher-throughput customers Direct Connect is recommended. The control plane can be in a separate management VPC; worker nodes are in the customer VPC if you opt for Private. Minimal public endpoints are used for rollout orchestration but can be restricted.
[02:03] Marco: How do you handle key management? We have strict KMS boundaries and sometimes HSM requirements.
[02:09] Samir: We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and have optional HSM integrations for FIPS/Higher compliance. Keys for model artifacts and logs can be customer-managed.
[02:20] Daniel: Good. On the go-to-market side, commissioning and margins — do you have a partner program, partner-level pricing discounts?
[02:29] Samir: Yes, we have tiered partner pricing — reseller margins increase with committed volume. For pilots we often do time-limited credits plus discounted pilot rates; if you convert to a committed Dedicated pool we can add co-sell funds. I'll send the partner deck after this.
[02:45] Priya: For pilot success metrics, we need latency P95 under 250ms for our chat use-case, and 90% availability during business hours. Also cost per 1k tokens needs to be comparable to alternatives.
[02:58] Leah: 250ms P95 is achievable depending on the model and quantization profile. Using a quantized LLM plus session KV cache and small continuous batching we can hit that for typical prompt lengths. We'll need your prompt distribution to model this.
[03:17] Priya: Yeah i'll share a sample prompt set and token histogram.
[03:21] Leah: Great. Also note routing policies: we can route live traffic to hosted models for latency-sensitive bursts and fall back to cheaper quantized variants on Dedicated when under load. That helps control egress and cost while maintaining performance.
[03:39] Marco: That sounds useful. On the security front, audit logs — how long do you retain them? Some regulators require 1 year, others longer.
[03:49] Samir: Default retention is 90 days, but enterprise packages include configurable retention (can be extended to 1 year or more) and we provide export hooks to S3 or your archive.
[03:59] Daniel: Any SOC2 or ISO attestation? We need to show that to partners.
[04:04] Samir: We're SOC2 Type II and have ISO 27001 in progress. I'll attach the security pack.
[04:11] Priya: Perf tooling — will we get per-route traces and token-level cost breakdowns?
[04:17] Leah: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost, traces, and eval hooks. For partners we can expose dashboards at the reseller level or provide partner-managed views.
[04:30] Daniel: Competitors we evaluated asked for tight single-tenant isolation; that was a pain point. How single-tenant is the Dedicated offering?
[04:41] Leah: Dedicated is single-tenant GPU pools; the control plane can be multi-tenant or customer-managed, depending on the Private option. For strict isolation you pick Private with a customer-managed control plane and your own KMS.
[04:53] Marco: What about model variants and quantization? I know we might want 8-bit quant for cost but worried about accuracy regressions.
[05:01] Leah: We recommend per-workload evals. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles; we tie regressions to prompt sets and can automate rollback if quality drops. For the pilot we can run a small A/B comparing fp16, 8-bit and 4-bit quantized variants.
[05:19] Priya: In terms of integration, what's the typical timeline for pilot — two weeks? a month?
[05:25] Samir: Typical pilot is 4–6 weeks to collect meaningful telemetry and customer feedback. Quick proofs-of-concept for basic functional tests can be 1–2 weeks if you use our hosted API.
[05:36] Daniel: Pricing for pilots and transition to committed — curious about minimum committed GPU hours or monthly spend.
[05:43] Samir: Depends on region/hardware but usually a small committed pool (e.g., 2x A100 equivalent) for a pilot. We'll map that to expected RPS and cost; the pilot credits offset setup. For long-term commits we have monthly reserved pricing.
[05:58] Marco: Can we run some workload-sensitive benchmarks? We use bursts of user traffic with long-context chat sessions.
[06:06] Leah: Absolutely. If Priya shares sample prompts and token distribution we'll simulate latency and throughput across candidate model families, batching configs, and KV cache strategies. We'll include quantization tradeoffs in the spreadsheet.
[06:20] Priya: Also need to verify data residency — some of our customers are EU-only. Do you have region controls?
[06:27] Samir: Yes, Redwood has regions in NA, EU, and APAC. For EU-only customers we can restrict deployments to EU regions and enforce data residency in the contract.
[06:38] Daniel: One question — on support and escalations how does that work for partners? Is there a partner SLA and a dedicated support channel?
[06:45] Samir: Partners at the reseller level get prioritized routing to partner success; for Dedicated deployments we offer SLA-backed uptime and a named technical contact. For larger deals we can provide a dedicated TAM.
[06:58] Priya: For the tech deep dive, we'd like Leah and a runtime engineer to look at our network diagram and pilot perf goals. Can we schedule that next week?
[07:06] Leah: Yes, i'll bring a runtime engineer. Week of Feb 9 looks open.
[07:11] Marco: Good. A small nit — licensing of model weights when reselling models, any issues?
[07:18] Samir: Models in our catalog are verified for redistribution in commercial settings where allowed; for custom or proprietary models you'll need to surface licensing constraints. We also support bringing-your-own-model (BYOM) for private deployments under different terms.
[07:34] Daniel: Okay, that's helpful. Anything else on the pilot metrics?
[07:38] Priya: We'll need a success criteria doc: latency P95 target, cost per 1k tokens threshold, error rates, and integration checklist.
[07:48] Samir: We'll draft a pilot success criteria template and include it with the pilot deck.
[07:55] Daniel: Sounds good.
[07:58] Samir: Quick recap — Samir to send partner deck and security pack; Leah to run perf estimate once Priya sends sample prompts; schedule SE tech deep dive week of Feb 9; Marco to introduce infra lead. Any blockers?
[08:15] Priya: None from our side, just need to coordinate the prompt set extraction.
[08:20] Marco: I'll loop Nina in.
[08:23] Daniel: Appreciate it, Samir. We'll review and follow up on the action items.
[08:27] Samir: Thanks all.
